\section[a garantia]{a garantia — the guarantee, the warranty}

\label{lesson:PT-C394-garantia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to transfer, then the Portuguese for the transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a garantia}
\textbf{a garantia} — \textquotedblleft{}the guarantee, the warranty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A máquina de lavar tem dois anos de garantia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The washing machine has a two-year warranty.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar na garantia} — to be under warranty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garantia} is usually traced to French \emph{garantie}, which EtymDB takes back to Old French \emph{garantie} \textquotedblleft{}protection, defence\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{garantir} and \emph{garant} \textquotedblleft{}guarantor\textquotedblright{}, a word with Germanic cousins such as Old High German \emph{werento} \textquotedblleft{}guarantor\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a garantia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a garantia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to transfer, then the Portuguese for the transfer, then say \emph{a garantia} again
\end{itemize}

\section[garantir]{garantir — to guarantee, to assure}

\label{lesson:PT-C394-garantir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the transfer, then the Portuguese for the guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: garantir}
\textbf{garantir} — \textquotedblleft{}to guarantee, to assure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Garanto-te que ele vem.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I assure you he is coming.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Garantir que} takes the indicative.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garantir} is usually traced to French \emph{garantir}, from Old French \emph{guarantir} \textquotedblleft{}to warrant, to vouch for\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{garant} \textquotedblleft{}guarantor\textquotedblright{}, a word of Germanic origin.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o reembolso]{o reembolso — the refund}

\label{lesson:PT-C394-reembolso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the guarantee, then the Portuguese for to guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o reembolso}
\textbf{o reembolso} — \textquotedblleft{}the refund\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pedi o reembolso do bilhete.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I asked for a refund on the ticket.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pedir o reembolso} — to ask for a refund.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reembolso} is built from \emph{re-} and \emph{embolsar} \textquotedblleft{}to put in your purse\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{bolsa} \textquotedblleft{}purse\textquotedblright{}, from Late Latin \emph{bursa} \textquotedblleft{}oxhide, purse\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the money goes back into your purse.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o crédito]{o crédito — the credit; the loan}

\label{lesson:PT-C394-credito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the refund, then the Portuguese for to refund.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o crédito}
\textbf{o crédito} — \textquotedblleft{}the credit; the loan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pedimos um crédito ao banco para comprar casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We asked the bank for a loan to buy a house.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Crédito à habitação} — mortgage. \emph{A crédito} — on credit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{crédito} came through Italian \emph{credito} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{crēditum} \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{crēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to trust, to lend\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
